The most common win left on "BIG BANK PAYDAY" is $10. The second biggest prize left is $50,000, and one of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything above about "BIG BANK PAYDAY" comes from the Virginia Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
2413.headline: What the prize table shows

2414.headline: A close look at the prizes

2415.body:
"Double The Money" is near the midpoint of its run, with about half of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, tickets are selling faster than top prizes are being claimed, which is good for the tickets that are left.

If "Double The Money" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
2415.headline: Early stage or late

2416.body:
"Loaded with $2,000s" is past the halfway point of its run, with about a third of its tickets still unsold. Late in a run, a game is worth a look when prizes outlast tickets. Early on, the prize design matters most. Here, the top prizes and the tickets are going at about the same pace.

If you play "Loaded with $2,000s" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.

2426.headline: Prize table details

2427.body:
"HOLIDAY TRIPLER" just went on sale in Virginia. The game has eleven full prize levels with 602 top prizes of $300. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.

2430.body:
